play: Commercial systems backlog and pipeline security directives
thesis: Enterprise Products is at record volumes, has raised its 2026 growth capex to $2.9-3.4B, and keeps adding assets (Bahia, Neches River, Occidental/Permian). All of that runs through an in-house .NET/SQL Server commercial application estate kept up by a lean team, under the TSA pipeline security directives. Devin adds capacity to extend, test and secure that estate without building up headcount, and Randy Fowler, who historically oversaw IT, becomes sole CEO in January.

why_now.t: Randy Fowler becomes sole CEO on Jan 4, 2027, and he has historically overseen IT. A new agenda window opens.
Growth capex was raised in July 2026, so more assets reach the commercial systems.
Acquired Occidental and Permian systems need integrating.
TSA SD-02 directives require prompt patching and segmentation.

challenges.stated: Record volumes and multiple new assets due through 2026-2027.
challenges.devin: Extend and test nominations, scheduling, measurement and invoicing apps for new assets in parallel.

challenges.stated: In-house .NET, SQL Server and Angular apps for core commercial operations, tracked in Azure DevOps.
challenges.devin: Fits the stack. Handles .NET upgrades, test coverage and documentation.

challenges.stated: TSA pipeline security directives: segmentation, monitoring, prompt patching.
challenges.devin: Code Scans and Security Swarm shorten time-to-patch, with evidence for audits.

challenges.stated: OT/ICS segregated; quarterly board cyber updates; no cyber insurance.
challenges.devin: Every Devin works in its own isolated machine and never touches OT. That lowers risk the company carries without insurance.

challenges.stated: Proprietary operational data is 'the new currency'.
challenges.devin: Data-pipeline and analytics engineering capacity for the Data Science team.

pain_chain.level: L1 CEO / CFO / Office of the Chairman
pain_chain.pain: Grow volumes and DCF while staying famously lean.

pain_chain.level: L2 Senior IT leadership at EPCO
pain_chain.pain: Commercial systems must scale with assets, and TSA compliance is ongoing.
pain_chain.measure: Time to onboard a new asset; patch SLAs

pain_chain.pain: A long-tenured, lean team carrying legacy .NET and stored-procedure code.
Stored procedures, .NET Framework upgrades, missing tests.

com.elevator: Record volumes and new assets keep landing on your in-house commercial systems, and TSA expects prompt patching. Devin is an autonomous AI engineer that extends, tests and secures those .NET apps in parallel, so the team keeps pace without adding headcount.
before: New assets queue behind a lean app team
Legacy .NET and stored procedures with little test coverage
Patching driven by TSA directives done by hand
negative: Commercial onboarding of new assets is delayed, which delays revenue
Compliance exposure with no insurance backstop
after: Asset onboarding changes shipped faster with tests
metrics: Days to onboard a new asset into commercial systems
